tasks.title: Industrial profile: model a lunch break with night factors
tasks.request:
Industrial profile: model a lunch break with night factors

Our plants stop between 12:00 and 13:00. `IndustrialLoadProfile.simple_profile` only knows a workday from `am`
to `pm`, so the break hour gets the "day" factor and the profile is too high around noon.

Could `simple_profile` take an optional break window (start and end time, like `am`/`pm`) during which the
"night" factors apply on workdays? Nothing should change when no break is given, and the result should still
integrate to the `annual_demand` I pass in, as it does today.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:31:47.861Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: Scale a BDEW 2025 profile to a given annual energy
tasks.request:
Scale a BDEW 2025 profile to a given annual energy

The new `G25`/`H25`/... profiles come normalised to 1 GWh per year in kW. Every user has to do the scaling by hand
and it is easy to get the factor wrong for non-quarter-hourly indexes.

Please add a way to get a 2025 profile scaled so that it integrates to an annual energy I specify (in kWh),
for any constant-step index the class already accepts. The unscaled behaviour must stay exactly as it is.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:32:26.348Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: Holidays given as datetimes with a time of day are not applied
tasks.request:
Holidays given as datetimes with a time of day are not applied

I build my holiday list from a calendar library that returns `datetime.datetime` objects at noon. Passing that
list as `holidays` to `add_weekdays2df` (or any of the profile classes) silently applies nothing: every holiday
keeps its ordinary weekday number and no warning is given.

Example: `holidays=[datetime.datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0)]` on a 2024 index leaves 1 January as weekday 1.
Passing `datetime.date(2024, 1, 1)` works. Holidays should match by date regardless of the time component,
for lists and for dicts.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:32:55.865Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: add_weekdays2df modifies the DataFrame it is given
tasks.request:
add_weekdays2df modifies the DataFrame it is given

`tools.add_weekdays2df(df, ...)` adds the `weekday` and `date` columns to the DataFrame I pass in, not only to
the one it returns. I reuse one frame for several scenarios with different holiday calendars and the columns
leak between them.

I would expect the input to be left alone and the result to be a new frame, or at least a documented way to
opt out of the in-place change. Existing callers inside the package must keep working.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:33:54.397Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: DeprecationWarning from DatetimeIndex.weekday when building profiles
tasks.request:
DeprecationWarning from DatetimeIndex.weekday when building profiles

With the current pandas, building any profile prints
`DatetimeIndex.weekday is deprecated and will be removed in a future version`, coming from the weekday
assignment in `tools.add_weekdays2df`. Our CI runs with warnings as errors, so this breaks the build.

Please use the supported accessor. Weekday numbering (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday, 0 = holiday) must not change.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:35:48.862Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.request:
Daily heat demand from HeatBuilding

tasks.title: Validate HeatBuilding inputs when the object is created
tasks.request:
Validate HeatBuilding inputs when the object is created

A typo in `shlp_type` (say "EFG") or a `wind_class` of 2 only blows up much later inside the sigmoid/weekday
parameter lookups with a KeyError or an empty-selection message that does not name the parameter.

Please check `shlp_type`, `wind_class` and `building_class` when `HeatBuilding` is constructed and raise a
ValueError that names the offending parameter and the accepted values. The existing rule that non-residential
types must use building class 0 must stay.

tasks.title: Industrial profile accepts overlapping day categories silently
tasks.request:
Industrial profile accepts overlapping day categories silently

Calling `simple_profile` with `week=[1,2,3,4,5,6]` and `weekend=[6,7]` is accepted. Saturday then gets whichever
factor the implementation happens to apply last, and the documentation says nothing about it.

Please raise a ValueError when `week`, `weekend` and `holiday` overlap, and when a weekday number outside 0..7 is
given. The default categories must keep working unchanged.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:40:37.739Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: Warn when an industrial profile is created with zero or negative annual demand
tasks.request:
Warn when an industrial profile is created with zero or negative annual demand

A unit mix-up gave us `annual_demand=0` and the industrial profile came back all zeros without a word; a
negative value produces a negative profile just as quietly.

In the spirit of the recent holidays warning, please emit a UserWarning for zero demand and raise a ValueError
for negative demand in `simple_profile`. Positive demand must behave exactly as before.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:41:22.149Z); fail at base, pass when solved

tasks.title: Derive the power conversion factor from the index resolution in ElecSlp
tasks.request:
Derive the power conversion factor from the index resolution in ElecSlp

`get_scaled_power_profiles` multiplies by a conversion factor that defaults to 4, which is only right for
quarter-hour data. When I resample to hourly first and forget the argument, the power is four times too high.

Please derive the factor from the profile's index frequency when it is not given explicitly (1 h → 1,
15 min → 4, 1 min → 60). Passing the factor explicitly must keep overriding it, and the quarter-hourly default
behaviour must not change.
tasks.notes: acceptance tests by gpt-5.6-terra at 6757f4f659 (2026-10-27T11:41:43.602Z); fail at base, pass when solved
